scenario.name: NCSC-NL, Talos & Mandiant — China-Nexus APT: FortiOS SSL-VPN & COATHANGER Persistent RAT
scenario.shortSubtitle: NCSC-NL / Mandiant / Talos · CVE-2022-42475 & CVE-2024-21762, preload.so Hook & smartctl Persistence
scenario.overview: Picture a grand central train station with an arched iron canopy, hanging station clock, ticket turnstiles, parallel railway tracks, and a sleek express train waiting at the platform. Beneath the central train station canopy, a stowaway slips past the platform ticket barrier using a copied conductor punch card right before boarding time. In this real-world scenario, the intruder steps up to the platform ticket barrier blending in with everyday guests, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the station conductor's station. The station master’s glowing track-indicator board flashes a route mismatch the instant the express train leaves its scheduled platform line. In this scenario (CVE-2024-21762, NCSC-NL, Talos & Mandiant, China-Nexus APT: FortiOS SSL-VPN & COATHANGER Persistent RAT) at 172.16.5.1, the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: heap Buffer Overflow in FortiOS sslvpnd, then hooking System Calls via /etc/ld.so.preload, then patching the flatkc Reboot Binary to Survive. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Heap Buffer Overflow in FortiOS sslvpnd, then Hooking System Calls via /etc/ld.so.preload, then Patching the flatkc Reboot Binary to Survive, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: FORTIOS SSLVPND HEAP OVERFLOW (CVE-2024-21762)
stages.subtitle: Unauthenticated out-of-bounds write in /bin/sslvpnd HTTP chunk parser
stages.description: Beneath the central train station canopy, a stowaway slips past the platform ticket barrier using a copied conductor punch card right before boarding time. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder steps up to the platform ticket barrier blending in with everyday guests while everyday visitors and the station conductor go about their routine. Against internet-facing FortiGate WAN self-IP 172.16.5.1, the attacker sends a specially crafted HTTPS request with a manipulated Content-Length header or encrypted parameter (enc) to the FortiGate SSL-VPN web endpoint (/remote/logincheck or /remote/hostcheck_validate, public VPN login pages reachable from the internet without prior authentication). This triggers a heap-based buffer overflow inside the sslvpnd daemon (writing attacker-controlled bytes past the end of the allocated heap buffer to overwrite adjacent function pointers in RAM and hijack the CPU into running the attacker’s code). In FortiOS, sslvpnd and almost all system utilities are compiled into a single monolithic multi-call binary (/bin/init). By chaining Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) gadgets inside that binary, exploiting sslvpnd gives the attacker immediate code execution inside the underlying Linux OS of the firewall. In the documented FortiOS Crashlog exchange from China-Nexus APT C2 to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK CVE-2024-21762 (confirming that the SSLVPND SIGSEGV request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 COATHANGER PRELOAD.SO ROOTKIT & SMARTCTL HOOK). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ SSLVPND SIGSEGV / ⇠#1 ACK CVE-2024-21762) from Node ① (#1 China-Nexus APT C2) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC NDR & Firmware Auditor).

stages.title: COATHANGER PRELOAD.SO ROOTKIT & SMARTCTL HOOK
stages.subtitle: Injecting preload.so into init and hooking /bin/smartctl for reboot survival
stages.description: Walking beside the railway tracks, the stowaway flips a track-routing switch lever so the express passenger train is redirected onto an unguarded freight siding. Here in Step 2 inside the train station, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the express passenger train without disturbing the eastbound local track. COATHANGER stores its backdoor files inside the persistent /data2/ partition and writes the path of its malicious shared library (preload.so) into /etc/ld.so.preload (a special Linux dynamic-linker configuration file that forces every single program launched on the system to load preload.so before the standard C library libc.so). Because preload.so is loaded first, it intercepts file-listing and process-listing calls (removing COATHANGER’s files and PIDs from the results so an admin inspecting the firewall sees nothing unusual). By hooking user-space libc functions like readdir(), open(), and stat() via /etc/ld.so.preload, whenever an administrator runs a diagnostic CLI command on the FortiGate, the hooked library filters out any path containing the implant’s directory before returning the output to the terminal. In the documented NCSC-NL YARA Match exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to FortiGate NGFW (sslvpnd), FortiGate NGFW (sslvpnd) responds with ALERT 36 KB ELF (confirming that the COATHANGER ROOTKIT request succeeded on FortiGate NGFW (sslvpnd) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 MASQUERADED HTTPSD BEACON & VPN CREDENTIAL THEFT). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ COATHANGER ROOTKIT / ⇠#2 ALERT 36 KB ELF) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 FortiGate NGFW (sslvpnd)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC NDR & Firmware Auditor).

stages.title: MASQUERADED HTTPSD BEACON & VPN CREDENTIAL THEFT
stages.subtitle: Exfiltrating VPN credentials and tunneling into internal Active Directory
stages.description: With the station clock ticking, the express locomotive pulls onto the alternate siding where unauthorized cargo bags are transferred off the rear coach. In this final step inside the train station, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the station conductor's station until the station master signal board catches the mismatch. Normally, rebooting a FortiGate or installing a FortiOS firmware update wipes the temporary root filesystem in RAM and loads a clean image. To survive both reboots and firmware updates, COATHANGER replaces /bin/smartctl and hooks the flatkc boot binary (the low-level FortiOS unpacker that initializes the filesystem whenever the appliance boots up, causing the firewall to automatically copy the hidden backdoor from the persistent /data2 flash partition back into the freshly updated system on startup). Because standard firmware upgrades replace the main rootfs image but preserve persistent flash partitions like /data2 alongside hooked boot components, simply installing a FortiOS patch without wiping and reformatting the appliance leaves COATHANGER active. In the documented Suricata TLS Alert exchange from FortiGate NGFW (sslvpnd) to COATHANGER (preload.so & smartctl), COATHANGER (preload.so & smartctl) responds with ALERT TLS 1.3 (confirming that the FORTIGATE EGRESS C2 request succeeded on COATHANGER (preload.so & smartctl) and completing the final execution objective of NCSC-NL, Talos & Mandiant, China-Nexus APT: FortiOS SSL-VPN & COATHANGER Persistent RAT). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ FORTIGATE EGRESS C2 / ⇠#3 ALERT TLS 1.3) from Node ③ (#3 FortiGate NGFW (sslvpnd)) to Node ④ (#4 COATHANGER (preload.so & smartctl)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC NDR & Firmware Auditor).

detectionRule.title: NCSC-NL Official YARA — COATHANGER FortiOS Implant
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule NCSC_NL_COATHANGER_Preload_Rootkit {
  meta:
    author = "NCSC-NL / MIVD"
    description = "Detects COATHANGER preload.so rootkit for FortiGate"
  strings:
    $p1 = "/data2/.bd" ascii
    $p2 = "/data/.bd" ascii
    $f1 = "/bin/smartctl" ascii
    $h1 = "readdir64" ascii
  condition:
    uint32(0) == 0x464C457F and ($p1 or $p2) and $f1 and $h1
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Because COATHANGER survives standard FortiOS firmware upgrades, compromised appliances must be wiped, formatted via physical console, and restored from clean backups.
